title: BPP execution_permit_consume request (DESIGN.md §13.1, §14.8; registry R34 runtime)
description: Mutation (meta required); an update — meta.expected_revision pins the exact authorized ActIntent revision (intent-revision CAS, RT-05): the one-shot decision is consumed against a pinned head, so a superseded or re-prepared intent fails stale_revision instead of consuming. One-shot consumption of an authorized ActIntent by the trusted host effect service bound to the exact prepared host Effect (R34): the host durably creates its local Effect with the same stable_execution_key first, REGISTERS it by minting host_effect_credential over {intent_ref, stable_execution_key, host_effect_ref, host_effect_digest} under the permit channel token byomd published for this act, then calls with that key, its exact host effect, the disclosure the act was authorized for, the budget set, the driver audience, and both current fences (§13.1 steps 3-4; byom_fence_epoch and host_fence_epoch are the derived dual-fence names — gap note G37). The member set is A8's, per member (PROFILE.md §6.2, R3-L01): byom's OWN recomputed digests are NOT members — intent_digest, subject_digest and episode_fence_digest were removed, because byom recomputes each from its committed ActIntent, act subject and ByomEpisodeBinding and publishes the committed value on the receipt, so an echo proved only that byom's value equals itself while costing the host per-object keyed digests it can never verify; and the digests byom DEMANDS from the host — host_effect_digest and disclosure_digest — are portable_public over frozen cross-boundary fragments, with host_effect_digest now VERIFIED rather than stored: it must re-derive from the frozen kovee-host-effect-binding-v1 fragment byom rebuilds out of its own committed act plus host_effect_ref, host_effect_external_idempotency_key and host_effect_request_byte_digest (R3-L01, D-R3-3), the same class effect_outcome_admit already requires for host_effect_digest, so the permit and the later outcome admission name the SAME value. BOTH host manifest bindings the act subject pins are exact pairs (context_manifest_ref with context_digest, disclosure_manifest_ref with disclosure_digest; each both-or-neither, closed oneOf arms, RT-05) and BOTH are compared, ref AND digest, against the pairs the gate seat assented to: the receipt renders byom's COMMITTED disclosure, never the presented one, and a context the consumption never presents is a context nothing binds — an act authorized under one ContextManifest is not consumable under another (R3-A01). Byom atomically rechecks charter, standing, Mandate, decisions, the locked Position revisions, dependencies, ceilings, expiry, and fences; inserts MandateUse; and returns one immutable ExecutionConsumptionReceipt (§13.1 step 5). Same semantic request and key -> same receipt; a changed request -> idempotency_mismatch over a frozen semantic-request digest covering EVERY substantive member (R3-A04); a different key cannot consume the spent one-shot decision (-> stale_revision); an unregistered or different host Effect -> forbidden; a stale fence -> stale_revision — vectors (G37).

stable_execution_key.description: The one-shot key minted at preparation; the host Effect carries the same key (§13.1).

host_effect_digest.description: The host's OWN commitment to the exact Effect it durably created for this act. portable_public over a frozen cross-boundary fragment (A8, PROFILE.md §6.2): byom holds the same bytes the host does, republishes them on the receipt, and effect_outcome_admit demands the identical value later — a keyed digest here would be an HMAC under the host's own per-object secret that byom could only echo.

host_effect_credential.description: The host-effect REGISTRATION authenticator (R3-A02): HMAC-SHA-256(permit channel token, $domain-tagged canonical `bpp-host-effect-registration-v0` fragment {intent_ref, stable_execution_key, host_effect_ref, host_effect_digest}), lowercase hex. The permit is bound to ONE exact prepared host Effect: byomd recomputes this value from the request's own members and the permit token it published `0600` for this ActIntent, and refuses (forbidden) before reading any state if it does not match. Without it the effect ref and digest were merely stored because a caller sent them, so a consumption could name a nonexistent Effect. It carries no key material: the token is byomd's own HMAC under its store key and is never derivable client-side.

host_effect_external_idempotency_key.description: The host's stable external idempotency key for this Effect, and a MEMBER of the frozen kovee-host-effect-binding-v1 fragment byom rebuilds (R3-L01, D-R3-3). It is not free: byomd re-derives it as `kovee-model-{stable_execution_key}-{host_effect_request_byte_digest.value_hex[0:16]}` and refuses anything else, so the two host-owned members are tied to each other and to the one-shot key byom minted.

host_effect_request_byte_digest.description: The §11.8 typed byte digest of the exact provider-request bytes the host sealed — the second and last member of the binding fragment byom does not already hold. With these two, byom rebuilds the whole preimage from its OWN committed ActIntent (intent_ref, stable_execution_key, and both assented manifest pairs) plus host_effect_ref, re-derives the portable_public digest and refuses a host_effect_digest that does not agree. Before it, host_effect_digest was ASSERTED: the registration credential authenticated a tuple CONTAINING the value, which proves who sent it, never what it is the digest of.

context_manifest_ref.description: The context manifest the gate seat assented to, presented again here. Compared — ref AND digest — against the pair committed in the act subject, exactly as the disclosure pair is: an act authorized under one ContextManifest is not consumable under another, and a consumption that presents no context for an act that pins one is refused rather than executed blind (R3-A01). The host owns the manifest, so the class is portable_public (A8).

context_digest.description: The exact content of that context manifest. The same reference carrying different content is precisely the substitution the pair exists to refuse, so ref and digest travel together or not at all (R3-A01).

disclosure_digest.description: The disclosure manifest the gate seat assented to, presented again here. Compared — ref AND digest — against the pair committed in the act subject, so the same reference carrying different content is refused instead of copied onto the receipt (R3-A01). The host owns the manifest, so the class is portable_public (A8).

episode_ref.description: The governed Episode this consumption runs inside; required for an external-effect act (family contract L21). Its ByomEpisodeBinding fence digest is byom's OWN record and is recomputed here, never presented (A8), so this reference no longer travels as a pair.

identifier.description: Opaque visible-ASCII identifier, at most 128 bytes (§14.9).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§14.2 rejects unsafe integers).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant with Z offset, semantically valid in the proleptic Gregorian calendar: the pattern pins the lexical ranges and implementations MUST additionally reject impossible calendar instants (e.g. 2026-02-30) — the conformance runner enforces this on every vector; leap seconds are not accepted. DESIGN.md does not fix a timestamp wire encoding; this derivation freezes with the bundle (gap note G3, amended per RT-17).

digestRef.$comment: The closed family DigestRef wire (family-vectors/PROFILE.md §6.1, normative; D-R0-1): exactly the members {class, algorithm, key_ref?, value_hex}. The oneOf pins the closed class/algorithm pairing and requires key_ref exactly for the keyed erasure classes; each arm refines members of this already-closed object.

class.description: Digest class (PROFILE.md §6, D-R0-1); substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.

key_ref.description: Key id for the keyed erasure classes; raw HMAC keys, per-object secrets, and salts are never part of a DigestRef.

digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef: every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash. Wire shape, class/algorithm pairing, and key_ref presence per the ratified family profile.

mutationMeta.description: MutationMeta (§14.2). Required on every mutation; this operation is update-classed (current-head CAS), so expected_revision — the last observed revision of the exact record head the operation moves — is REQUIRED (closed update meta; RT-01). Omitting it fails the closed schema; the server compares it against the current head and a stale value fails stale_revision.

portableBindingDigest.description: Contextual digest-class binding (PROFILE.md §6.2 cross-boundary class rule, amendment §A8; RT-02): this field commits to a FROZEN cross-boundary fragment the consumer holds and must re-derive without a byom secret, so exactly class portable_public (unkeyed SHA-256 over the $domain-tagged canonical fragment) is acceptable. A well-constructed digest of any other class here is digest_class_mismatch — and a keyed one would be a value the consumer could only echo, which is the defect the rule exists to prevent.
